facts: Sacra independently summarizes H1 2026 revenue at $23.4M, up 74% year over year, with Q2 revenue at $13.5M after the August revenue-recognition revision.
Sacra reports government customers at approximately 83% of H1 2026 revenue and the U.S. government at 74%, providing independent support for material customer-concentration risk.

Sacra reports remaining performance obligations of $22.5M at June 30, 2026, with $8.9M expected in H2 2026 and $12.5M in 2027; reaching approximately $45.1M 2026 guidance therefore requires continued execution and incremental bookings beyond disclosed backlog.
Sacra notes the August revision shifted revenue previously recognized in 2024 and 2025 into 2026 without changing underlying contract economics or cash flow.
risks: Government/customer concentration remains high, increasing sensitivity to program timing and procurement execution.
Full-year guidance is not fully covered by disclosed remaining performance obligations and requires continued contract execution plus incremental bookings.
Revenue-recognition revisions increase the value of cash-flow and contract-level corroboration when Alpha constructs numeric underwriting.
contradictions: Strong reported revenue growth coexists with concentration and backlog coverage that leave execution risk material.
unknowns: This independent source does not by itself establish normalized gross margin, customer-level contract durability, or a complete valuation input set.
